reaction_name: SNAr of 4-fluoronitrobenzene with piperazine to give 1-(4-nitrophenyl)piperazine

feed_streams.reasoning: Electrophilic substrate dissolved in DMF; kept separate from nucleophile until mixing point to avoid premature reaction at room temperature
Nucleophile feed; slight excess (1.2 equiv) to drive conversion; concentration set so that equal volumetric flow rates of A and B deliver correct stoichiometry

reagents.name: 4-fluoronitrobenzene
reagents.notes: Para-nitro group strongly activates the ipso carbon toward nucleophilic attack; fluorine is the best leaving group in SNAr due to high C–F bond polarity and stabilization of Meisenheimer complex

reagents.name: piperazine
reagents.notes: Bis-nucleophile; 1.2 equiv used to drive mono-arylation; excess beyond ~1.5 equiv risks double arylation to give 1,4-bis(4-nitrophenyl)piperazine as byproduct

reagents.name: DMF (N,N-dimethylformamide)
reagents.notes: Polar aprotic solvent stabilizes Meisenheimer complex and solvates fluoride leaving group; do not exceed 150 °C to avoid decomposition to dimethylamine and CO

mechanism_steps.description: Nucleophilic addition: piperazine N–H attacks the ipso carbon (C-1) of 4-fluoronitrobenzene bearing the fluorine, forming the anionic Meisenheimer complex (sigma complex). The para-nitro group delocalizes the negative charge onto the oxygen atoms of the nitro group, stabilizing the intermediate.
Elimination: fluoride ion departs from the Meisenheimer complex, restoring aromaticity and generating 1-(4-nitrophenyl)piperazinium fluoride (protonated product) and fluoride anion.

Proton transfer: the piperazinium N–H proton is transferred to fluoride (or to a second piperazine molecule acting as base), yielding neutral 1-(4-nitrophenyl)piperazine and HF (or piperazine·HF salt).

key_intermediate: Meisenheimer complex: anionic sigma complex formed by addition of piperazine nitrogen to C-1 of 4-fluoronitrobenzene, stabilized by para-nitro group resonance delocalization

stream_logic.reasoning: Electrophilic substrate in DMF; pumped at flow rate F_A to deliver 1.0 equiv relative to piperazine stream

Nucleophile in DMF; concentration set to 0.36 M so that equal volumetric flow rates of A and B give 1.2 equiv piperazine relative to substrate; equal flow rates simplify pump control and give combined substrate concentration of 0.15 M post-mixing

mixing_order_reasoning: Streams A (4-fluoronitrobenzene in DMF) and B (piperazine in DMF) are combined at a T-mixer or chip mixer at the reactor inlet. Mixing at room temperature before the heated coil is acceptable because SNAr is negligibly slow below ~60 °C; no exotherm risk at the mixing point. The combined stream then enters the heated coil at 120 °C. Piperazine must not be pre-mixed with DMF at high temperature for extended periods to avoid any N-formylation side reaction with DMF.
deoxygenation_reasoning: Batch protocol run under air with no adverse effect; SNAr mechanism does not involve radical intermediates or metal catalysts sensitive to O2; deoxygenation is unnecessary.
quench_reasoning: No reactive intermediates requiring inline quench; standard aqueous workup post-collection is sufficient to remove piperazine·HF salt and DMF.
